newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks low, trade hit by automation trials.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks low, trade hit by automation trials.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed a shade low on Wednesday in trade which was hit by automation trials launched to test screen-based trading, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.6 points down at 728.5. Price gains and declines were 30 to 28. Ceylon Tobacco fell two rupees to 40, Cold Stores five to 125.
Turnover was 90.4 million rupees, up from 30.3 million rupees on Tuesday.
"Turnover was up as it was possible to trade, since buyers seemed willing to pay premiums for selected shares," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
Buyers were forced to pay premiums for shares of companies which have seen good corporate profits in the year to March and the first quarter of 1997, brokers said.
They also said automation trials launched on Tuesday to test a new screen-based trading system slowed proceedings.
The Public Enterprise Reform Commission, which oversees privatisations, meanwhile said it will sell 51 percent of Namunukula Plantations, at 40 rupees a 10-rupee share on Thursday.
